entry.title: Catacombs of Paris

groundCutout.basis: Clip the terrain below both modeled shaft landing pads, including the René-Coty side room. PMTiles paving is retained.

buildingCutout.basis: Reuses the independent public-portal footprints and replaces the low former Fontis exit frontage. The taller rear volume behind the former outlet remains mapped.

entry.note: The draft ties the galleries to the independently mapped public portals and the former Fontis frontage. The complete public route, shaft positions and full Fontis street connection remain estimates.

review: The Paris Musées diagram and three PMTiles controls locate the approximate return toward René-Coty and the guided Fontis branch. The draft’s 775 m public centerline remains shorter than the museum’s listed 1.5 km itinerary. The two registered portal placements retain their elevations and nearby paving. The full underground placement remains a draft.

tuileriesMemorial.modeledLocation: Estimated wall position along the draft route between the French Revolution memorials and the Crypt of the Passion.
tuileriesMemorial.note: The museum guide establishes the tour sequence. The street portals share their current map anchors. The combined model is still a draft and the memorial’s underground position is estimated.

sacellum.limitations: The Sacellum uses the museum photograph for the stepped altar and the arrangement of the three tablets. Its chamber, wall side and distances are estimated between the Samaritaine and the lamp. Small lettering is unresolved.

martyrsMarker.scope: The close-up includes the Greek and Latin lines, dedication and year. The master adds the French translation, Homer citation and small date lines. The stylized strokes and marker dimensions are interpreted. The photograph does not locate the wall in geographic coordinates.

guideRoadAxes.conclusion: The street axes in the visitor diagram and PMTiles meet at different angles. A uniform scale and rotation cannot align both axes. Exact gallery coordinates still require underground survey controls.

aqueduct.interpretation: The registry identifies the surface feature as access shaft 25. The inscription identifies the stretch between shafts 24 and 25. The measured distance checks their relative neighborhood without fixing the wall position.

ossuary.interpretation: The museum describes about 800 m of walking after the threshold. The diagram-based model covers a shorter route through this section. The positions of the missing route sections remain unresolved.

exitShaftPlanCheck.observation: The exit cutaway puts the spiral inside the room to the right of the street passage. The modeled landing ends toward the central passage through a side doorway. The footprint constrains the modeled rim, while its precise center and the room dimensions remain estimated.

entryDepthInscription.scope: The April 2026 photograph shows the HAUTEUR depth inscription. Its position along the entry gallery and the dimensions of its stone panel are estimated. The historic number is reproduced on the sign. The current floor elevation follows the draft terrain and route controls.

easternOssuaryGallery.interpretation: The 2025 plan depicts the eastern and southern ossuary legs. The English guide routes the visitor toward the Crypt of the Passion via the eastern leg. The model represents the connection as an additional gallery. The 775 m through-route measurement uses the southern branch.
easternOssuaryGallery.limitation: The museum plan shows an additional east ossuary leg between the northern junction and the Crypt of the Passion approach. Its size, exact bearings and current direction of visitor travel remain estimated.

rueHallePlaque.credit: Eric Emo / Musée Carnavalet – Catacombes / Roger-Viollet
rueHallePlaque.captionEvidence: Two lines of shallow serif carving on a pale stone inset in the reinforcement wall.
rueHallePlaque.limitation: The museum photograph records the incised Rue Hallé plaque in a quarry reinforcement wall. The model places it in the lower approach near the PMTiles street crossing. The actual passage location, wall side and plaque dimensions remain estimated.

denfertLandingRoom.observation: The Denfert axonometric section shows a turn from the visitor corridor through a walled approach room to the head of the spiral.
denfertLandingRoom.model: The model adds plaster partition walls and a framed doorway inside the fitted annex at the upper landing datum.
denfertLandingRoom.limitations: The Denfert stair approach uses a short enclosed room and open doorway, based on the architect’s cutaway. The door, shaft and partition positions within the footprint remain approximate.

reneCotyGalleryReturn.comparisonAttachment: Annexe 6 · Plan des galeries, scénario parcours, option 2
reneCotyGalleryReturn.planningSourceType: Public preview of a Paris Musées route planning attachment
reneCotyGalleryReturn.geometryBasis: The Paris Musées planning diagram marks the bends toward René-Coty and a separate guided branch toward the former Fontis exit. The revised draft follows the exit-side return and joins the Fontis gallery there. Registration uses both public portals and the Fontis address. Exact junction geometry and final as-built underground positions remain estimates.

controlTiepoints.name: Fontis former exit at 36 rue Rémy-Dumoncel

reneCotyGalleryReturn.limitation: The draft public centerline measures 775.2 m. The Paris Musées planning trace measures about 785 m when fitted to the two public portals and former Fontis address. The museum lists a 1.5 km visit. The difference remains unresolved.
